title: I rebuilt my digital nomad life sim in Three.js with AI coding tools. Here's what worked and what didn't
author: albertsimondev
selftext:
VybeNomad is a free, cozy browser game. You pick your base city, take remote gigs, build little apps and travel, trying to reach $10,000 before you burn out.

How AI fit in:

* AI wrote most of the Three.js code. It was fast for UI and game state, but the city scenes needed a lot of fixing by hand.
* Balancing was the hard part. The AI was happy to suggest numbers, but only playtesting showed that early gigs paid too much and players hit $10k way too fast.
* What I'd do differently: put all the game numbers in one config file from day one, instead of letting the AI scatter them across the code. Tuning would have been much faster.

Music is by Suno and the art was made with fal.ai.

Play it here (free, no signup, works on phones): [vaigames.com/vybenomad](https://vaigames.com/vybenomad/)

How do you balance an economy sim when AI writes most of the code?
